title: Module injective resolutions compute derived abelian presheaf inclusion
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the common sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use ordinary $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $U:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ for forgetting scalars, $\operatorname{PAb}(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Ab})$, and $\iota:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ for inclusion, right adjoint to abelian sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The three abelian categories have enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms and $D^+$ for the full bounded-below derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Compute $R\iota$ on bounded-below abelian injective resolutions, with its canonical natural comparison $\alpha_L:Q(\iota L)\to R\iota(QL)$.
For every $M\in\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ there exists a degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism $r:M[0]\to I^\bullet$ with injective module terms and $I^n=0$ for $n<0$. For every such $r$, the terms $UI^n$ are $\iota$-acyclic, meaning $R^q\iota(UI^n)=0$ for $q>0$, and the comparison
$$c_r=(R\iota(Q(Ur)))^{-1}\circ\alpha_{UI}:Q(\iota UI^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\iota(UM[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D^+(\operatorname{PAb}(\mathcal C))$.
For any nonnegative abelian injective resolution $s:UM[0]\to J^\bullet$, there exists a chain map $b:UI^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ satisfying $b\circ Ur=s$. Any two such maps are homotopic; $\iota b$ is a quasi-isomorphism and, under the injective-resolution identification $Q(\iota J^\bullet)\cong R\iota(UM[0])$, its derived image is $c_r$.
If $f:M\to N$ is a module map and $r':N[0]\to I'^\bullet$ is another resolution of this kind, there exists a chain map $\widetilde f:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ with $\widetilde f\circ r=r'\circ f[0]$, any two lifts are homotopic, and
$$c_{r'}\circ Q(\iota U\widetilde f)=R\iota(Uf[0])\circ c_r.$$
For $f=\mathrm{id}_M$ this identifies the comparisons for any two choices of resolution. Under the kernel identifications induced by $Ur$ and the abelian resolution augmentation, $H^0(c_r)$ is the identity of $\iota UM$. No finite-product, subcanonical, flatness or finite-cover hypothesis is imposed. No assertion that $UI^n$ is injective as an abelian sheaf is made.

source.place: Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), acyclicity proof; derived.tex Tag 015E (lemma-leray-acyclicity), Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift), Tag 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy). Agent formulation as a normalized isomorphism of derived presheaves.

proof.text: Use the existing Grothendieck-abelian instance on ordinary module sheaves and enough injectives [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist, lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Abelian sheaves also have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. For M take Mathlib injectiveResolution M and its integer extension I.cochainComplex with augmentation I.ι'. The negative objects are zero, all terms injective, and the augmentation a quasi-isomorphism. Its degree-zero component is monic by InjectiveResolution.ι'_f_zero; every other component has zero source. This constructs exists_resolution.

Forgetting scalars U preserves finite limits and finite colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], so preserves monomorphisms and quasi-isomorphisms. Inclusion ι preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise]. Evaluation E_W on abelian presheaves is exact by objectwise limits and colimits [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-colimits-sectionwise]. Consequently R^q(ι ⋙ E_W)(A) is naturally isomorphic to (R^qι(A))(W): compute both on the same injective resolution and commute the exact E_W with homology (Functor.rightDerivedCompObjIso). By [lem-sc-site-cohomology-right-derived-sections] the former is H^q(W,A). For injective modules I, [lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski] makes these groups zero in positive degree. Objectwise zero implies zero presheaf; hence every UI^n is ι-right-acyclic.

Apply the existing acyclic-unit theorem [src-right-derived-functor-plus-acyclic-unit] directly to UI. The given α_UI is invertible, and its composite with Rι(Q(Ur)) inverse is exactly comparison ι (Ur). This proves module_resolution_derived_presheaf_comparison without resolving UI again. The same theorem on any supplied abelian injective resolution J gives invertibility of comparison ι s, because injective abelian objects are right-acyclic.

For a commutative square r ≫ t = f ≫ r' of bounded-below complexes with quasi-isomorphisms r,r', naturality of rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit and functoriality of Q and Rι yield Q(ιt) ≫ c_r' = c_r ≫ Rι(Qf). The localization of r is precisely qIso r hom: fully faithful inclusion in the unbounded derived category reduces this to the definition of Qh. Cancel Rι(qIso r') hom to verify the equation using only naturality and inverse identities. This is the proved private comparison_naturality helper.

Use the degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism Ur and target J in [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] to obtain strict b with Ur ≫ b = s. Any two such b are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy]. Two-out-of-three makes b a quasi-isomorphism. Its source and target have inclusion-acyclic terms, so [lem-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity-quasi-iso] makes ιb a quasi-isomorphism. For arbitrary bounded-below bounds use their minimum. Apply the naturality helper with f=id to obtain Q(ιb) ≫ c_s = c_r. This proves all clauses of abelian_resolution_comparison.

For a module map f, apply the same strict lift lemma to r and f[0] ≫ r', now in module sheaves. Homotopy uniqueness follows from the same bounded-below injective-target theorem. Apply U to the strict square and then the comparison_naturality helper to prove module_map_comparison for every lift. For identity_comparison specialize f=id. The lift is a quasi-isomorphism by its augmentation equation; U preserves it by exactness, and ι preserves it by [lem-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity-quasi-iso] since both forgotten resolutions have acyclic terms. Simplify the naturality formula on the identity.

For a quasi-isomorphism between complexes zero below zero, the short complex at degree zero has zero incoming differential. Any left exact additive functor preserves its left homology: Functor.preservesLeftHomology_of_zero_f identifies it with the preserved kernel. Thus ιUr and ιs induce H0 isomorphisms. Transport to derived homology using homologyFunctorObjQIso_hom_naturality. Write a=H0(Q(ιUr)), a'=H0(Q(ιs)), c=H0(c_r), c'=H0(c_s). The strict lift equation and Q(ιb) ≫ c_s = c_r give a ≫ c = a' ≫ c'. Set e_r=(singleH0(U ⋙ ι,M)) inverse followed by asIso a, and e=(singleH0(U ⋙ ι,M)) inverse followed by asIso a' and H0(asIso c_s). Their homs are exactly the two prescribed augmentation identifications. Cancel e hom to deduce e_r hom ≫ c ≫ e inv = id. This proves degreeZero_normalization. The kernel preservation uses the already cited exactness of U and finite-limit preservation of ι.

lean.statement: theorem module_resolution_derived_presheaf_comparison (M : ringedSiteModules.{u} (ring J R)) (r : Resolution (single M)) : (∀ n : ℤ, (sheafToPresheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u}).rightAcyclic ((forget J R).obj (r.complex.obj.X n))) ∧ IsIso (comparison (sheafToPresheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ((forget J R).mapCochainComplexPlus.map r.augmentation))
lean.note: The six theorem declarations together state every clause of the node. The main declaration gives inclusion-acyclicity and the canonical derived-category comparison; companions give existence, comparison with every abelian resolution, lift uniqueness, naturality, resolution independence, and augmentation-normalized H0. Resolution retains arbitrary Z-indexed supplied complexes. Helpers are transparent uses of existing constructions and the explicit canonical comparison, not arbitrary maps.

reviewed_lean.note: First S2 delivery; only lean differs from live; record complete and statement verbatim. comparison = Mathlib rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit followed by the inverse of RF(qIso r); qIso.hom = Plus.Q.map r, so the map is canonical. Main theorem: termwise rightAcyclic (q+1, no injectivity claimed) and IsIso c_r for every r. Abelian-resolution lift/homotopy/quasi-iso/Q(ιb)≫d_s=c_r, module-map naturality for every lift (order checked), identity case and degree-zero normalization with both identifications fixed to the augmentation maps all match the node. The Resolution structure is exactly the node's four conditions on ℤ-indexed complexes. No extra hypotheses or universe equalities; edge cases checked; defs real; all theorems sorry; docstrings and imports OK. Maintainer note: rightAcyclic is def-sp-acyclic's recorded declaration, which the node defines inline; adding it to stmt_deps is optional.
